title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: section (30) of the continuation of La Longue Marche (manuscript pp. 748-749), 'Enveloppes schématiques d'un T-L-groupe profini, a) les enveloppes admissibles'.

The objects are as follows.
- M is a profinite 'T-L-groupe' (a profinite group with loop/Teichmüller structure, typically an arithmetic fundamental group of a moduli space or curve over a number field).
- M comes with a structural character χ_M : M → Ẑ^* whose image is open.
- π is a defining subgroup, a profinite 'groupe à lacets', i.e. the geometric part.
- π_0 ⊂ π is a discrete 'discretification' whose profinite completion is π (e.g. a discrete surface or mapping-class group inside its completion).

The previous page fixes an affine group scheme G_Q of finite type over Q and the ring A_Q = Ẑ⊗Q of finite adèles, with G(A_Q) ⊂ ∏_ℓ G(Q_ℓ).

This page does three things.
- If G_Q extends to a finite-type group scheme G over Z, then (25) G(A_Q) is the restricted product: (x_ℓ) with x_ℓ ∈ G(Z_ℓ) for almost all ℓ.
- One adds a character (26) χ_G : G_Q → G_{m,Q}.
- One studies group homomorphisms (27) M → G(A_Q) satisfying a list of axioms.

Axiom 1° (continuity) is restated as two conditions:
- (a) each component M → G(Q_ℓ) is continuous;
- (b) for ℓ outside a finite set S, it factors continuously through (28) M → G(Z_ℓ).

Grothendieck notes that this condition does not depend on the chosen Z-model, and that (28) is a map of profinite groups.

The next page completes the list.
- Re-NB: one can choose the model so that the whole map factors through G(Ẑ).
- 2°: compatibility of χ_M and χ_G via Ẑ^* ⊂ A_Q^*.
- 3°: a finite-index subgroup of π_0 maps into G(Q) (the Q-rational structure).
- 4°: minimality / irredundancy, i.e. no proper subgroup G'_Q works (Zariski density).

Purpose: to define a 'schematic envelope' of an arithmetic fundamental group. This is a Q-algebraic group, together with a cyclotomic-type character, receiving M adelically (all ℓ at once), with the discrete topological group π_0 landing in Q-points. In other words, an adelic, Q-rational analogue of Malcev / Zariski-closure completions, aimed at the Galois action on Teichmüller towers.
errors: No real error on this page. The equivalence in 1° is correct for this reason: M is compact, so its image in the restricted product is compact, hence lies in some ∏_{ℓ∈S}(compact) × ∏_{ℓ∉S} G(Z_ℓ). Conversely, (a)+(b) give continuity into the restricted-product topology.
Independence of the Z-model is correct, since two models agree over Z[1/N].

The next-page claim that the model can be chosen with factorization through G(Ẑ) needs an argument. It holds by taking an M-stable lattice in a faithful representation at the finitely many bad primes and the schematic closure there. It is stated tentatively ('Si j'en crois').
The adèles used are finite adèles only (no archimedean place). This is deliberate but unstated on this page.
Next-page diagram: the bottom-left target should be Ẑ^* rather than Ẑ, and the product is written ∏_{ℓ≠p}, which is inconsistent with ∏_{ℓ∈P} here. These are minor notational slips.

ideas.what: Adelic points of a Q-group as a restricted product relative to a Z-model, independent of the model
Continuity of a profinite group homomorphism into G(A_f) is equivalent to continuity at each ℓ plus integrality at almost all ℓ ('unramified almost everywhere'-type condition)
ideas.modern_name: continuous adelic representation / compatible system integrality

ideas.what: Schematic envelope of a profinite arithmetic fundamental group, built from three ingredients: a Q-group G with character χ_G : G → G_m, an adelic homomorphism M → G(A_Q) compatible with the cyclotomic character, and the discrete geometric subgroup π_0 mapping into G(Q), all subject to minimality
ideas.modern_name: adelic analogue of weighted completion / relative completion; algebraic (Mumford–Tate-type) hull of Galois actions on fundamental groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, fundamental group of P^1 minus 3 points); Hain (relative completion, 1990s); Hain–Matsumoto (weighted completion, 2003)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only gestures at the Galois–Teichmüller tower, not at this construction (as far as I know)

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines admissible 'schematic envelopes' of a profinite T-L-group M. These consist of a Q-group G with χ_G : G → G_m and a homomorphism M → G(A_f), compatible with χ_M, sending a discrete model π_0 into G(Q), and minimal. It is an adelic, Q-rational, all-primes-at-once version of what later appeared ℓ-by-ℓ as Hain–Matsumoto weighted completion and Hain's relative completion of mapping class groups.
missed.quote: On se donne de plus un hom. (26) G_Q --χ_G--> G_m Q. On s'intéresse à des homomorphismes de groupes (27) M → G(A_Q) satisfaisant à des propriétés que nous allons énumérer.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Weighted and relative completions are usually done one prime ℓ at a time, over Q_ℓ. Grothendieck's axioms (adelic continuity, χ-compatibility, π_0 → G(Q), minimality) ask for a single Q-group controlling all ℓ simultaneously, with a rational structure coming from the topological fundamental group. This is close to motivic-Galois / Mumford–Tate-type expectations for Galois actions on π_1 of moduli spaces. Questions of existence and uniqueness of such minimal envelopes for M = π_1 of M_{g,n} over Q do not seem to be formulated in this form in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This page alone is routine (restricted product, continuity). However, it sets up an unpublished, axiomatic, adelic notion of 'schematic envelope' with a cyclotomic character and a discrete Q-structure that anticipates weighted/relative completion (Hain, Hain–Matsumoto, 1990s–2003). That is a notable unpublished detail, but the idea family is well developed later, so it is not deeply surprising.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads '· schéma de t.f. G sur Z, dans ...', continuing 'Si G_Q provient d'un schéma en groupes affine de t.f. G sur Z, dans ce cas ...'.
In (25) the condition reads 'x_ℓ ∈ G(Z_ℓ) pour presque tout ℓ' (Grothendieck writes Ẑ_ℓ, meaning Z_ℓ).
In 10) a), the target is written G(Q_ℓ) over a corrected letter (first written as A?).
In (28), G(Ẑ_ℓ) means G(Z_ℓ), the ℓ-adic integers.
The item is '1°) Continuité' (the next page refers to 'propriété 1°)'), not '10)'.
This page sits between manuscript pages 748 and 749 and continues 748; '201' is the archive scan number.
